live_qa.final_build_followup: After the live calls, a deterministic guard was added for an analogy whose own scope explicitly limits it to a shared purpose. The old Transformer file was correctly rejected by strict import. Its captured draft was replayed through the final validator, then both surviving maps were opened, inspected and exported in the offline UI, without another provider call. Request prompts, retrieval and provider contracts were unchanged.
diagnostic_quality_findings: A pre-scope PECVD run retained a SiGe-to-GaN application with mismatched materials.
Scope prompts alone still admitted weak cross-paper applications and analogies; common-source admission was added afterward.
Recent applications crowded foundations out of an ancestry query. Source diversity and earlier atlas evidence were reserved.
Substring matching admitted unrelated source candidates, including question-word matches inside longer words; whole-word matching and query coverage were added.
The last Transformer draft still included a shared-purpose analogy; the final guard withheld it during offline replay.
These are observed draft-quality failures, not erased or relabeled as verified knowledge. Surviving draft interpretations may still be wrong.

limitations: Personal maps remain unverified drafts. Automated checks and model criticism are not qualified human scientific review.
The bounded scholarly-index and atlas retrieval is not a complete web search or a reconstruction of all historical ancestry.
A common source is an admission prerequisite, not proof of the connection. This conservative rule also omits some valid cross-paper links.
Provider delays and source failures vary. Time estimates are heuristic; successful runs do not guarantee future availability.
Keys persist only when explicitly selected. Checkpoints remain session-only; saved partial maps are inspectable but cannot resume on their own.
Corpus coverage is unchanged and below the expansion targets. No new qualified human audit or frozen research-suite rerun was performed.
macOS and desktop/mobile-emulated Chrome were tested. Windows, Linux and physical phones were not tested in this local upgrade.
